title: The Portrait of Greywater Bay
premise: Ines Pemberton, the quiet archivist of Greywater Bay's cathedral, is forced into the open when the town's founder, Aldous Vane, is exhumed for a centenary ceremony and his coffin proves empty. Following a trail of forged burial records, hidden letters, and a second grave beneath the crypt floor, Ines uncovers a conspiracy among the town's founding families who staged Vane's death to cover his murder. As the conspirators close in to protect their legacy, Ines must choose between preserving the archive he loves and exposing the truth, ultimately testifying before a hostile town and finding, in the witnesses who stand with him, the family he never had.
about_author: Paloma Dravenmoor spent a decade cataloguing parish records in coastal towns before turning to fiction, and her prose carries the dust and patience of the archive. She writes mysteries about people history tried to file away and forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dust
chapters.summary: Ines Pemberton's POV. Ines catalogs the cathedral crypt ahead of the centenary exhumation of founder Aldous Vane, establishing his invisible life among the town's elite and his quiet bond with verger Marisol Cruz. When the coffin lid is lifted before the assembled dignitaries, it holds only river stones. The beat: shock cracking open a carefully sealed existence.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Lies
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The mayor demands discretion while Ines quietly checks the burial register and finds the 1924 entry written in ink that didn't exist until decades later. Someone altered the record after the fact. Marisol warns him that the founding families guard their dead jealously. The beat: the first thrill of discovery shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with an interlude letter from Vane's daughter, Eleanor. Searching tidal archives, Ines learns Vane drowned twice—once in official record, once in a fisherman's testimony never filed. He tracks down the fisherman's granddaughter, Odette, who possesses her grandfather's suppressed account. The beat: grief for a man erased, and the first ally beyond the cathedral walls.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Ines and Odette's POV alternating. Beneath the crypt's oldest flagstones, they find a shallow unmarked grave holding Vane's remains—and evidence of violence: a fractured skull. Before they can document it, someone seals the crypt and reports them for desecration. The beat: triumph curdling into accusation; Ines becomes suspect instead of seeker.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Silence
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. Suspended from his post, Ines works through Odette as they interview descendants of the four founding families. Each family carries a fragment: a burned letter, a missing servant, a hushed quarrel over Vane's will, which left everything to the town rather than to his partners. The beat: the conspiracy takes shape—greed dressed as civic virtue.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Box
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A dying elderly woman, Vane's last living descendant, gives Ines her grandmother Eleanor's box: letters proving Vane discovered his partners were smuggling and exploiting dockworkers, and that he planned to expose them days before his 'drowning.' The beat: righteous fury; justice reframed as something owed to the powerless.

chapters.title: Ash Wednesday
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The conspirators' heirs burn a wing of the cathedral archive to destroy corroborating records. Ines races through smoke to save what he can, badly injured, saved by Marisol and Odette—the found family crystallizing around him. One arsonist is caught and, terrified, names names. The beat: loss and loyalty intertwined; the case turns.

chapters.title: The Long Confession
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The caught arsonist confesses: the founders killed Vane and staged the drowning, then buried him beneath their own monument. But the statute of limitations has expired, and the town's institutions close ranks. Legal justice is impossible. Ines realizes the truth must be given to the people, not the courts. The beat: despair transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Vigil at Greywater
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. On centenary night, Ines opens the crypt publicly, lays out Vane's bones and the evidence, and reads Eleanor's letters aloud to the gathered town as the conspirators' heirs try to stop him. The crowd, descendants of the exploited dockworkers, refuses to look away. The beat: the climax—truth spoken in the house that hid it.

chapters.title: A New Register
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Months later, Vane is reburied with honors, the founding families' names struck from civic monuments, and the archive rebuilt with Odette and Marisol at Ines's side. Justice came outside the law, but it came. Ines writes a new first page in the restored ledger—his own name, no longer invisible. The beat: belonging, earned and recorded.
